title: Kachemak south-shore lakes test (59.541 N, 151.203 W) -- lake-basin prior review, 1 m
note: Test composite set up 2026-10-10 at Hig's request: a setting with several datasets, partial overlap and real gaps. Grid is a snapped 1 m lattice on NAD83(2011)/UTM 5N covering China Poot Bay, Peterson Bay and the Halibut Cove entrance (x 595-606 km, y 6602-6610 km), chosen so that the three-way overlap of Grewingk 2021, KBay 2023 and the Hydropalooza bathymetry (around Halibut Cove) and the two-way KBay + bathymetry case (China Poot Bay) are both inside. Sources are datasets.json ids, read from the archive COGs, all NAVD88 (GEOID12B); the 2009 bathymetry carries its -1.38 m MLLW shift. The KBay 2023 layer is the landslidescience reclassification (kbay_2023_reclass), not the vendor DEM: the vendor COG has a compound NAVD88 CRS that gdalwarp geoid-shifts on full-resolution reads (see CLAUDE.md), and the reclass is the preferred bare earth. Classes: the bathymetry is bed everywhere (gridded from soundings with no interpolation across unsurveyed ground, so there is no TIN hull to reject); Grewingk 2021 (12 Oct) gets the lake-level detector and a snow guess against KBay 2023; KBay 2023 gets the reclass's own fill_mask (2 = harmonic fill, classed modelled), a flat-below-level detector for the sea surface it holds at several tide levels (-3.0..-1.9 m NAVD88 on different lines, plus +0.8), and a compare-to-bathymetry step for water over known bed. `lowest` is on for KBay against Grewingk at region scale: the two lidars differ by +0.58 m median over 31 km2 of overlap (KBay higher), which is canopy, and the lower of two sound DTMs is the better ground. Grewingk 2021 carries shift_m +0.36 (see its notes).

layers.name: ctx3dep
layers.notes: Fallback everywhere: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second seamless (~10 m; IfSAR-derived in Alaska), the same data Mapterhorn serves in Alaska (median difference 0 m against this bake, reference_mapterhorn) -- read locally rather than from Mapterhorn's tiles. NAVD88. Date a nominal 2012 (IfSAR era); sigma 3 m, so any survey outranks it and it shows only where nothing else does. Its lakes are hydroflattened: class ground here, so where it is the only data a lake reads as a flat surface -- the class axis from the surveys above still says water there.
layers.class_notes: 2026-10-11 (Hig: China Poot Lake read as a short steep drop to a flat floor): the fallback step makes 3DEP void wherever any survey has a cell, whatever its class -- its hydroflattened lakes sat ~5 m below KBay's water level and stood in for the bed once water stopped being a surface, so the hole fill never saw the lakes. Bilinear: ~10 m cells read nearest at 1 m were stair-steps. Footprints: the two lidars' point-class rasters (valid wherever a tile was flown), so open water a survey flew over and kept nothing from is a hole, not 3DEP's sea surface (Halibut Cove Lagoon: 3DEP at 0 m between the multibeam lines).

layers.name: bathy2009
layers.notes: H11933-38 (2008) and H12084-12146 (2009); mid-2009 as the date. Per-band native cells 1-8 m stacked on a 1 m VRT.

layers.name: grewingk2021
layers.notes: shift_m +0.36: MEASURED 2026-10-10, not from metadata. On bare smooth flat ground (both DTMs < 0.05 m rough, slope < 3 deg, 2-20 m: beaches, flats, fans) KBay 2023 reads +0.36 m above Grewingk 2021 with NMAD 0.06 m (n 108k at 2 m), while KBay reads +0.014 m (NMAD 0.048) against Seldovia 2019 NCMP topobathy, the survey the 2009 bathymetry's MLLW->NAVD88 shift was tied to, and the reclass matches the vendor DEM to 1 cm. Two independent products against one: Grewingk sits ~0.36 m low in the collection's NAVD88(GEOID12B) frame despite its metadata. No third witness overlaps it (Homer 2019 and Lower Kenai have no data over it). Belongs in datasets.json as vertical_shift_m for hosting to apply after its own check; applied here explicitly so the test composite has no 0.4 m seam at Grewingk's edge.
layers.class_notes: 2026-10-10: classes from the point cloud (observe_points.py, rules 'grewingk': ground where the DTM has a value and real returns exist, water = DGGS class 9, void where only noise); replaces the DEM-derived water_level + snow_vs steps. With all 119 tiles the vendor ground class covers 93-99% of DTM cells in every band to 1100 m, so there is no class-based hook for a snow hypothesis; snow on 2021-10-12, if any, is inside the ground class.

layers.name: sonar2023
layers.notes: Katie Hughes' Grewingk Lake sonar (gated; NAVD88 GEOID12B from the LAS headers). Not in this box -- listed so the stack is the same everywhere it is used.

layers.name: kbay2023
layers.notes: flight dates to confirm (NOAA says 2023, delivery 2023/24); mid-2023 assumed CLASS from the point cloud (observe_points.py, 2 m): ground where the reclass DTM has a value and the cell has returns; VOID where the laser got no returns (the bay, lagoons, lakes) and where the reclass filled (its fill_mask) - Hig 2026-10-10: the fill is meaningless, mask it out; water where class-9 returns outnumber ground (checked: flat, sparse, at -2.9..-2.3 m or the 50 m lake); built where class 6 outnumbers ground; snow from class 21.
layers.source_notes: Box mosaic of the reclass rerun (water rules + structures) until kbay_2023_reclass is republished.

layers.name: dixon2023
layers.notes: Mark Laker (USFWS Kenai NWR) SfM, 19 Sep 2023, converted to NAVD88/GEOID12B at ingest (datasets.json). A SURFACE model: over vegetation it is canopy, so it must not outrank lidar ground -- sigma 0.5 vs the lidars' 0.15 keeps it underneath wherever they have ground; it shows where it is the only survey. Its water surfaces carry the lake levels on 19 Sep 2023. Its datum against grewingk_2021 (measured -0.02 at 700-1100 m by hosting, against our +0.36 on low flat ground) is unresolved.

layers.name: fill
layers.notes: The hole interpolation (composite.py fill, topobathy/fill.py): a context-aware prior (shore bands from the rim slope, low-tide floor) conditioned by the soundings. Class modelled, so it stands in at half rank under water/bed and never where a real observation exists; sigma from fill_sigma.tif (grows from the shore, relaxes near soundings). Optional: skipped until the fill has been run; 'composite.py fill' treats the cells it won as holes, so build -> fill -> build is idempotent.

fill.notes: Lakes review box. Lake parameters at their defaults (lake_vd 0.5, hollister_k 0.5, lake_water_frac 0.5). Sparse depths: 'points' = Nick's July 2018 lake soundings (China Poot Lake 157, the 67 m lake 82; Hazel lakes outside the box), z = KBay water level - depth (see the README beside the CSV).

notes: Lake-basin review box (Hig, 2026-10-11: 'near 59.54106, -151.20282 where there are a number of lakes of different sizes'): ~60 lakes 0.5-105 ha. Stack = every survey that covers it, oldest first, over a 3DEP fallback: Hig asked why the Grewingk Lake box had used neither Mark Laker's SfM (dixon_2023) nor Katie Hughes' sonar (grewingk_sonar_2023) -- the recipe was a copy of Kachemak's, whose box neither reaches; a recipe lists its layers by hand, so a box needs its own survey search (wanted: an 'auto' layer list from the catalogue footprints).
margin_m_notes: 2026-10-11: margin_m 0.05 -> 0. With equal sigma (0.15) the older Grewingk 2021 kept every cell it reached and the newer KBay showed only where Grewingk's class raster was void -- i.e. at the edges of the LAZ tiles classified for this box, straight km and half-km lines with a 0.1-0.3 m step. At 0 the newer survey wins a tie.
